title: Imam Bayildi Stuffed Eggplant

description: Imam Bayildi is a truly divine Turkish dish featuring whole eggplants stuffed with a rich, aromatic filling of onions, tomatoes, garlic, and herbs. Slow-cooked in olive oil, this vegetarian delight offers a symphony of sweet and savory flavors. It is traditionally served cold or at room temperature, making it a perfect mezze or light main course.

ingredients.notes: about 1.5 kg total, peeled in stripes
or to taste, plus more for eggplants

instructions.title: Prepare Eggplants
instructions.text: Slice the eggplants lengthwise, but not all the way through, creating a pocket. Sprinkle generously with salt and let them sit for 30 minutes to draw out bitterness. Rinse thoroughly under cold water and pat dry with paper towels.

instructions.title: Fry Eggplants
instructions.text: Heat about 1/4 cup of olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Fry the eggplants in batches until golden brown and softened, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove and place on paper towels to drain excess oil.

instructions.title: Prepare Filling
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another splash of olive oil if needed. Sauté the chopped onions over medium heat until translucent and softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Cook Filling
instructions.text: Stir in the diced tomatoes, sugar, salt, and pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes, until the tomatoes soften and release their juices. Remove from heat and stir in the fresh parsley and dill.

instructions.title: Stuff and Arrange
instructions.text: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Carefully open each eggplant pocket and generously fill with the prepared onion and tomato mixture. Place the stuffed eggplants snugly in a baking dish.

instructions.title: Bake Imam Bayildi
instructions.text: Pour 1/2 cup of hot water into the baking dish around the eggplants. Drizzle the remaining 1/4 cup of olive oil over the stuffed eggplants. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until eggplants are very tender and the sauce is slightly reduced.

instructions.title: Serve
instructions.text: Allow Imam Bayildi to cool completely before serving, as it is traditionally enjoyed at room temperature or chilled. Garnish with extra fresh parsley or dill and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice, if desired.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, use good quality extra virgin olive oil generously. It's a key component of this dish.
Salting and draining the eggplants is crucial to remove bitterness and ensure they absorb less oil during frying, resulting in a silkier texture.
Imam Bayildi is best served at room temperature or even chilled the next day, allowing the flavors to meld beautifully. It makes excellent leftovers.
article:
Imam Bayildi: The Sultan of Stuffed Eggplant – A Turkish Vegetarian Delight

Dive into the heart of Turkish cuisine with a dish so legendary, its name translates to "the Imam fainted" – likely from sheer delight at its exquisite flavor. Imam Bayildi is more than just a stuffed eggplant dish; it's a symphony of slow-cooked vegetables, rich olive oil, and aromatic spices that culminates in a truly unforgettable vegetarian experience. Originating from the Ottoman Empire, this classic meal showcases the beauty of simple ingredients transformed into something extraordinary. If you're searching for an authentic taste of Turkey that's both healthy and satisfying, mastering the Imam Bayildi recipe is a must. Get ready to embark on a culinary journey that will tantalize your taste buds and leave you craving more of this magnificent Turkish vegetarian staple.

## What is Imam Bayildi?
Imam Bayildi is a traditional Turkish dish featuring whole eggplants generously stuffed with a savory mixture of onions, garlic, tomatoes, and herbs, all slowly braised in olive oil. It's a prime example of *zeytinyağlı* (dishes cooked with olive oil), a category of Turkish cuisine typically served cold or at room temperature, perfect for mezzes or light main courses. The dish's rich, complex flavors develop over a long, slow cooking process, allowing the eggplant to become incredibly tender and absorb all the aromatic juices.
